The award-winning high street is packed with independent shops, cafes, bakeries and delis. Ramsbottom even boasts its own brewery with tap room, which is just a stone's throw away from the apartment, a live music venue and a theatre. Our little town has become famous in recent years for its thriving food and drink scene. You can enjoy everything from Thai to tapas, with some of the North West's very best pubs and restaurants just a few steps away.

The most popular local walk is to Peel Tower at the top of Holcombe Hill, which will reward you with amazing views. Chorlton has an effortlessly great vibe, and it is not hard to realise why. Away from the busy city centre, it is filled with independent restaurants, bars, cafés, and shops, and has been named one of the coolest places to live in the Manchester area. The selection of bars and restaurants here is second only to the city centre – so if you love the social aspects of living in the heat of it but cannot afford the sky-high rents, this one is for you.

Chorlton covers a large area, so there is plenty of housing stock – mostly in period homes and apartments. In the summer, residents spill out onto the streets to enjoy the sunshine or take strolls through the local nature reserve. It feels miles away from the city centre but hop on a tram and you will be at St. Peter’s Square within 15 minutes – a real 'best-of-both-worlds' situation.

name: City Centre Location - Unique Romantic Canal Boat
description:
💙 WELCOME TO FLOATING HOMESTAYS 💙

An adorable pet-friendly, romantic hideaway in heart of Manchester. Quirky interior inspired by 1950’s Havana. Showpiece is an honesty bar with wine, spirits & cigars. neighborhood_overview: We’re situated in the heart of Castlefield and a stones throw away from Deansgate, the Museum of Science and Industry, The Crystal Maze, Spinningfields, Deansgate Locks and the Hilton Hotel. The tram is a 7 minute walk from the boat and there are free buses along Deansgate. We’re situated next to the city’s historic ruins and have a couple of small beautifully kept parks surrounding us. The boat is also parked in the Castlefield bowl where they often host live music events. This area is a public space and so it can be festive at times. There are also some pretty vocal geese in the spring months and you can hear the trains passing overhead. If you're sensitive to the sounds of the city then this is not the place for you. Ear plugs provided.

host_about:
Hi, I'm Amanda! 

My own travels have taken me to set up home in various places from Manchester and Yorkshire to Spain but I've lived in Wigan now for over 7 years. I have a love of animals, nature, good music and good food and would like to offer you a warm welcome to the home of the Verve, the Wigan International Jazz Festival and (of course) the annual World Pie Eating Championships. 

I joined other fellow Wigan hosts in late 2021 to offer locals and travellers a change of scenery from the regular hotel spaces on offer as well as the opportunity for travellers to perhaps stick around a little longer to see what the historic town of Wigan is really all about. From Real Ale and Cider to the Fairy Glen, from classic British food to international cuisine, the northern treasure of the ancient Haigh woodland park and the Museum of Wigan Life, where George Orwell did the research for his book 'The Road To Wigan Pier'. There are little gems all over the town to discover and you have the perfect base to do just that. 

A warm welcome to all and please get in touch if you have any questions, I'll do my best to accommodate individual needs.

Happy travels! :)

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Monton Village is a lovely suburban neighbourhood. It has a wide variety of independently owned cafes, bars and restaurants, all within a 2-minute walk of our property. some of our favourite places for food include Playfoots Cafe Bar and La Turka, or Vintage Ambiance for amazing cocktails! There are also a couple of chain stores, for convenience, such as Tesco and Costa Coffee, as well as a Post Office.

There are some beautiful walks nearby, including the trail to Swinton, or the woods and meadows past Monton Green. It is an extremely friendly, quiet and safe neighbourhood with lovely people!
host_about:
My name is Robbie (the guy on the right) and I live with my husband, Scott (the other one). We share our house with our beautiful dog, Nikko. He is a Japanese Akita, and he is a gentle giant, but a little grumpy sometimes! He will only be roaming free when we’re in, and if we’re out, he will be in our room.

We love cooking, going to the cinema and having a good time. Meeting new people is important to us and because of this, socialising, hosting parties and spending time with friends are things that we value.

We are confident and outgoing individuals that embrace new experiences. Road trips to different cities are great and we love traveling the world, having recently toured the East and West Coast of America. We love adventures as well as spending quality time together.

We are secretly geeky, with a love of sci-fi movies and Doctor Who. We do, however, love to party as well. If we're heading on a night out, it will be somewhere playing House or Electro tunes. We can be found in a quiet bar doing a pub quiz, or in a mega club, dancing all night. We're pretty easy going when it comes to a fun night out and we're happy to try new venues or music styles.

In a nutshell: we're chilled, fun and happy people living by the motto, "Here for a good time, not a long time!"

Eccles is a quiet neighbourhood in Manchester, offering excellent transport links directly into the City Centre, being within a 15 min drive.

Historically, Eccles grew around the 13th-century Parish Church of St. Mary where a textile industry was established during the Industrial Revolution, the area is also famous for the Eccles cake.

Today the neighbourhood is leafy and green, providing an ideal base within a peaceful and tranquil environment offering an escape from the hustle & bustle of Manchester City, whilst being close to all local amenities popular for tourists, contractors, corporates, and residents alike.

Monton is an upmarket area within 5 mins drive, popular with visitors due to the trendy bars, restaurants, coffee shops and nightlife that can be found here, with plenty of walks along the canals and converted disused railway lines.

Tram: West Didsbury has its own Metrolink stop on the South Manchester line. Trams run frequently into Manchester city centre, with journey times of around 15 minutes.

Bus: Several reliable bus routes run through the area, including the 43 (direct to Manchester Airport), 142, 111, and 147, offering quick access to the city centre, hospitals, and the university.

Train: The nearest railway station is East Didsbury, just a short drive or tram ride away, with direct trains to Manchester Airport and Manchester Piccadilly.

Airport: Manchester Airport is only 6 miles away, about 15 minutes by car or 35 minutes
